input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Inventory: the whiteboard shows CloudFront, S3 (static web app), Cognito, Sanofi SSO, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Service Catalog, R Studio (on EC2), SageMaker, Lambda, Translate, Comprehend Medical and an S3 Data Lake. The two S3 icons have distinct roles (static website vs. data lake), so they stay separate. The generic users icon is pruned; CloudFront is the system entry point. CloudFormation is only mentioned as the templating mechanism behind Service Catalog products, so it is not a node. 2) Portal flow: CloudFront (holds the certificate, reduces cost) serves the S3 static website; users are authenticated via Cognito federated with the Sanofi SSO. 3) Dynamic/traceability flow: the web app calls API Gateway, which writes user metadata and all portal actions to DynamoDB. 4) Provisioning flow: from the portal, users provision products through Service Catalog, which deploys R Studio (EC2) and SageMaker notebooks per user. 5) ML flow: Lambda functions use the SDK to call Comprehend (automatic language detection and Comprehend Medical entity identification) and Translate (bulk translation of raw files to a user-chosen target language). 6) Data Lake: the audio states that data is extracted into the user's home S3 bucket and then processed in R Studio, SageMaker, Translate or Comprehend. No arrows are drawn for this on the board, so the Data Lake edges to EC2, SageMaker and Lambda are inferred from the audio only. No trigger for Lambda is drawn or described, so none was added.

graph.name: Sanofi Darwin: Secure Data Science Portal for Real World Evidence Data
graph.categories: Machine Learning, Analytics, Data Lake, Healthcare, Security
graph.notes: Sanofi and Teamwork built a secure data analytics portal on AWS for data scientists working on Real World Evidence data in the Darwin ecosystem. Static web portal on S3 behind CloudFront, authentication through Cognito federated with the Sanofi SSO, traceability through API Gateway and DynamoDB, self-service provisioning of R Studio and SageMaker through Service Catalog, and translation / medical NLP through Lambda with Translate and Comprehend Medical. Sensitive data stays in the environment in a segregated S3 Data Lake with one home bucket per user. In production since early August; grew from 5-10 beta testers to 30-40 users in 2-3 weeks. Lake Formation is being considered for the future.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Distribution in front of the static website; used to reduce costs and holds the certificate. Entry point for the portal users (data scientists).

nodes.name: S3 — Static Web App
nodes.notes: Static web portal (Data Analytics portal) hosted with the S3 static website feature.

nodes.name: Cognito
nodes.notes: Authenticates portal users through identity federation with the Sanofi SSO.

nodes.name: Sanofi SSO
nodes.notes: Sanofi corporate single sign-on; identity source federated with Cognito.

nodes.name: ApiGateway
nodes.notes: Dynamic part of the portal; used to implement data traceability.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: User activity log: stores user metadata and all actions performed on the Data Analytics portal; strong traceability of each piece of data used in the environment.

nodes.name: ServiceCatalog
nodes.notes: Portfolio of products (SageMaker and R Studio) that users provision from the portal. Products are built with CloudFormation for repeatable, secure, per-user isolated deployments.

nodes.name: R Studio
nodes.notes: R Studio (proprietary app) running on EC2; one machine per user, provisioned through Service Catalog, with access only to that user's own data set.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: SageMaker Notebooks provisioned through Service Catalog; encrypted, with a 100 GB disk for data, traced, one notebook per user with access only to that user's own data set.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Lambda functions that call Translate and Comprehend through the SDK for bulk translation of raw files and identification of data/metadata in raw files.

nodes.name: Translate
nodes.notes: Bulk translation of raw files from an automatically detected source language to a target language chosen by the user.

nodes.name: Comprehend Medical
nodes.notes: Comprehend is used to automatically detect the source language; Comprehend Medical specifically is used to identify data/metadata within raw files (NLP).

nodes.name: S3 — Data Lake
nodes.notes: Data Lake holding very sensitive data that must stay in the environment and cannot be downloaded to a workstation. Each user has their own home bucket; data is segregated, encrypted, audited and accessible according to predefined rights.

edges.notes: CloudFront serves the static web portal hosted on S3.
The web portal authenticates users with Cognito.
Cognito federates identities with the Sanofi SSO.
The dynamic part of the portal calls API Gateway for traceability.
API Gateway stores user metadata and all portal actions in DynamoDB.
From the portal, users provision products through Service Catalog.
Service Catalog provisions a per-user R Studio machine (CloudFormation-based product).
Service Catalog provisions a per-user encrypted SageMaker Notebook with a 100 GB disk (CloudFormation-based product).
Lambda calls Comprehend through the SDK to detect the source language, and Comprehend Medical to identify data/metadata in raw files.
Lambda calls Translate through the SDK to bulk-translate raw files to the target language chosen by the user.
Data extracted into the user's home bucket in the Data Lake is processed in R Studio (stated in the audio, not drawn).
